subhead: 'Room for Hope' (2/6). While too many European forests have been turned into timber factories through monoculture and clear-cutting, the Swiss Confederation is testing an ancient technique that encourages cooler conditions and greater biodiversity.

title: Gaza's children forced to put away their kites after Israeli threats
subhead: After several kites from the enclave were discovered on the Israeli side, authorities, seeing a potential threat, announced that anyone flying a kite would be targeted. Many Palestinian families chose to confiscate these toys – one of the few pastimes left – from their children.

title: 'Under Trump, pursuing a project on Israel and Palestine at university is an institutional ordeal'
subhead: In this op-ed, American art historian and professor of Judaic Studies Katharina Galor describes how an exhibition of drawings by Palestinian and Israeli children has sparked debate at Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island, where she teaches.

title: Southern France village devastated by tornado: 'It was like bombs were dropped on our heads'
subhead: Pomas, a village of 1,000 people, was struck by a violent tornado on Monday, August 24. Although only around 50 people were injured, nearly two-thirds of the village's 500 houses suffered severe damage.

title: The Suez Canal: Birth and death of a colonial myth
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (1/6). In 1869, the creation of a maritime route linking the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, operated by the French and the British, captivated Europe. Initially a symbol of colonial oppression for the Egyptian people, the waterway became a tool of emancipation when President Nasser announced its nationalization 70 years ago, on July 26, 1956.

title: Retro 'sunflower' pools bring nostalgia to Paris region and beyond
subhead: 'Aquatic Monuments' (5/6). The Tournesol pool, an emblem of prefabricated and modular architecture, spread throughout France in the 1970s, leaving its mark on generations of swimmers with its flying saucer-like appearance. Built in 1976, the Raymond-Mulinghausen pool in Les Lilas, on the edge of Paris, still welcomes swimmers in an almost unchanged setting.
